# Astra's Patch Steward Milestone Plan

**IMPORTANT NOTE:** This plan was generated by by ChatGPT Astra. It is for comparison only as a different perspective on the development path. Nothing in this plan is to be used in the implementation.

## Purpose and basis

Deliver version 1 of Patch Steward: help contributors prepare supportable issues
and pull requests, screen them before substantive maintainer review, and measure
whether screening reduces total maintainer work without systematically excluding
valid contributions.

The starting point is a development scaffold, not an implemented screening
service. The architecture governs components and trust boundaries; the processes
govern behavior; the whitepaper supplies methodology and goals. These milestones
define capabilities, inputs, outputs, dependencies, and acceptance conditions.
Detailed designs, algorithms, interfaces, command syntax, and numerical defaults
belong to implementation work within each milestone.

## Scope and completion rules

Version 1 covers GitHub issues and pull requests in public and private
repositories; contributor preflight; maintainer local screening; historical
replay; GitHub-hosted screening; a static submission assistant and dashboard;
repository installation; and measured rollout. Both specified inference providers,
Copilot SDK and OpenAI-compatible services, are included. The selected architecture
has no hosted backend.

Separate security-report intake, AI-authorship detection, automatic merging,
active comment moderation, cross-repository duplicate matching, and tool-enabled
model agents are outside this release. Security-claimed issues follow the
project's escalation policy without automated severity judgments.

Every milestone must satisfy these common conditions:

- Demonstrate its outputs against representative success, rejection, uncertainty,
  failure, and changed-input cases applicable to that capability. Preserve
  previously completed behavior.
- Keep the trusted policy authoritative. Submission content and model output
  cannot grant permissions, change policy, or decide final outcomes.
- Keep foreign code isolated from credentials and the host. Distinguish
  contributor claims, steward evidence, and external CI signals; isolation does
  not guarantee honest test results.
- Never report a screening pass when required evidence or required work is
  missing. Distinguish contributor corrections, maintainer decisions, service
  failures, and nonterminal waiting states.
- Bind decisions to their inputs and retain an auditable explanation. Record
  relevant usage, latency, failures, and lifecycle events from the first working
  capability, not only during final evaluation.
- Respect repository visibility and authorized disclosure. Keep private evidence
  private unless an explicitly authorized subset may be published.
- Update user-facing documentation with the delivered behavior and limitations.
  Resolve prerequisite decisions before dependent work relies on them.

A milestone is complete when its outputs exist and its completion criteria are
demonstrated. A document describing a capability is not a substitute for that
capability. Dependencies below identify required completed milestones; preparatory
work may overlap when it does not assume unavailable outputs.

## M01 — Trusted policy and submission contract

**Goal:** Make a repository's contribution requirements explicit, enforceable,
and understandable before any expensive screening work begins.

**Inputs:** Project requirements and process definitions; existing scaffold;
representative repository policies, issue drafts, and PR drafts.

**Outputs:**

- Working policy validation and revision identification, covering supported
  behavior, categories, evidence requirements, escalation, modes, disclosure,
  and resource limits.
- Deterministic submission checks with specific correction requests, including
  ambiguous templates, category mismatches, missing evidence, and sensitive
  changes. Proposed policy changes remain subject to the current trusted policy.
- Common outcome, report, evidence, and measurement behavior that subsequent
  capabilities can use consistently; policy validation and local report viewing
  are available to users.
- A representative acceptance-case collection covering valid contributions,
  unsupported claims, proposals, malicious content, and unavailable dependencies.

**Completion criteria:** A maintainer can validate a policy and inspect contract
results for issue and PR examples. Invalid policies are surfaced without silent
fallback. Incomplete submissions produce actionable corrections without inference
or submitted-code execution. Category ambiguity cannot relax required screening.

## M02 — Bounded inference, retrieval, and execution

**Goal:** Provide the controlled services needed to examine untrusted submissions.

**Inputs:** M01 policies and acceptance cases; authorized provider access;
representative repositories and supported execution environments.

**Outputs:**

- Both required inference providers, with explicit selection, capability checks,
  validated responses, usage reporting, and consistent failure outcomes.
- Bounded retrieval of repository context, references, and reproduction material,
  subject to visibility and disclosure rules.
- Isolated local execution of foreign code and generated tests, with identifiable
  environments, bounded results, and clear evidence provenance.
- Cumulative resource accounting, redacted local evidence, and visible handling of
  unavailable environments, refusals, malformed responses, and exhausted budgets.

**Completion criteria:** Controlled hostile-input exercises demonstrate the
required credential, execution, and disclosure boundaries. Models cannot invoke
tools or choose permissions. Required service failures cannot become passes.
Provider changes never occur silently; unsupported usage or cost information is
reported as unknown, and soft spending limits are described accurately.

## M03 — Evidence-backed issue screening

**Goal:** Determine whether an issue provides a supported defect claim or a
well-formed proposal before it consumes substantive review effort.

**Inputs:** M02 services; issue snapshots; trusted requirements; supported-version
information; references, reproductions, and relevant prior repository decisions.

**Outputs:**

- Reference verification that distinguishes confirmed absence from inability to
  verify, with findings tied to the claimed revision and project applicability.
- Claim classification with supporting evidence, duplicate/prior-dismissal
  context, and explicit handling of new evidence on previously dismissed claims.
- Reproduction results for applicable supported versions and maintenance targets,
  distinguishing behavioral failure from environment failure.
- A local issue report that routes defects, intended behavior, duplicates,
  proposals, uncertainty, and security claims according to policy.

**Completion criteria:** Representative cases reach the documented outcome for
the documented reason. A defect does not pass without required reproduction.
A well-formed unaccepted proposal enters the proposal backlog without implying
intent acceptance or requesting unnecessary author corrections. A supported
release defect is not dismissed merely because another target is already fixed.

## M04 — Complete pull-request assessment

**Goal:** Establish that a proposed change addresses a justified claim and meets
the project's verification requirements.

**Inputs:** M03 claim validation; PR snapshots and linked issues; declared tests;
project requirements, mandatory checks, platform expectations, and CI signals.

**Outputs:**

- Category-specific PR assessment, including current linked-issue validation,
  proposal requirements, and the distinction between accepted intent and technical
  correctness.
- Before-and-after fix evidence and integrated verification, with findings for
  incomplete fixes, weakened tests, and execution-sensitive changes.
- Regression analysis that distinguishes introduced failures, pre-existing
  failures, instability, and unavailable required platform coverage.
- Independent challenges grounded in trusted expectations and assessed without
  author reasoning; findings distinguish demonstrated violations from suggestions.
- A consolidated local decision and report with evidence, unmet requirements,
  maintainer questions, and what would change the outcome.

**Completion criteria:** Cases include valid fixes, tests that fail for the wrong
reason, incomplete fixes, introduced regressions, intentional behavior changes,
unrequested feature changes, and missing coverage. Mandatory checks cannot be
removed by model judgment. Advisory findings cannot block alone. Reused evidence
matches all relevant inputs and retains its provenance.

## M05 — Contributor and maintainer local workflows

**Goal:** Make the screening capabilities useful on contributor and maintainer
machines before automatic repository feedback is introduced.

**Inputs:** M04 screening; target repository policies; local drafts and branches;
user credentials where needed.

**Outputs:**

- Contributor preflight with deterministic checks, local verification previews,
  a default checklist when no target policy is published, and optional
  model-assisted self-review after disclosure and confirmation of the material
  being transmitted.
- Maintainer screening of remote issues and PRs with local evidence and reports.
- Explicitly requested, attributed local publication; experimental local policies
  and contributor preflight results remain distinguishable from official results.
- Documented local setup, authentication, report inspection, and failure recovery.

**Completion criteria:** A contributor completes deterministic preflight without
an inference account. A maintainer screens foreign code safely and can inspect
the resulting evidence. Preflight does not write to GitHub. Local publication
requires an explicit request and never satisfies the official repository gate.

## M06 — Historical replay and evaluation baseline

**Goal:** Evaluate screening quality without influencing live submissions or
leaking known answers into screening.

**Inputs:** M05 local screening; labeled historical issues and PRs; authorized
historical context; explicit policy revisions and evaluation cutoffs.

**Outputs:**

- A replay workflow using frozen historical inputs, with outcome labels and
  later information withheld from screening.
- A documented evaluation collection containing valid and invalid issues, valid
  fixes, incomplete fixes, and regressions, with coverage gaps identified.
- Baseline reports for false admissions, valid contributions blocked,
  inconclusive cases, decisive stages, latency, usage, and cost where available.
- Repeatable comparisons between steward versions, policies, and providers,
  with limitations from missing context and possible model familiarity reported.

**Completion criteria:** Replay neither refreshes cases with hindsight nor writes
to live submissions. Missing historical inputs remain visible in results. Issue-only
evidence is not presented as validation of patch verification. The initial baseline
is recorded before feedback-enabled live evaluation begins.

## M07 — GitHub screening in observation mode

**Goal:** Run the complete screening process automatically on repository activity
while collecting evidence without changing the normal review process.

**Inputs:** M04 assessment; authorized test repositories and GitHub identity;
provider access; trusted policy; target-repository visibility rules.

**Outputs:**

- Event-driven screening of issues and PRs with hosted isolation and credential
  boundaries equivalent to the local screening guarantees.
- Durable official evidence in either supported store location, with authorized
  access, retention, redaction, supersession history, and private maintainer views.
- Current-input ownership, duplicate suppression, dependent rescreening, and
  recovery from interrupted work, missed events, and partial publication.
- Repository capacity controls, aged queued and inference-approval states,
  maintainer admission/rerun support, bounded retries, and model-availability
  reporting.
- Observation-mode outcome and workload records, including closures, reopens,
  and bounded audit samples, without report comments, state labels, or reviewer
  requests.

**Completion criteria:** Public and private test repositories produce durable,
current evidence through normal and failure scenarios. Changed submissions,
linked issues, consumed author responses, and policies invalidate affected work;
unchanged duplicate events preserve useful work. Closed submissions are not
admitted. Queued or held work is recoverable and visible even with Pages disabled.

## M08 — Contributor feedback and maintainer control

**Goal:** Return unfinished work to contributors and give maintainers a concise,
auditable way to resolve uncertainty and disputes.

**Inputs:** M06 baseline; M07 hosted screening and evidence; feedback-enabled test
policies; contributor responses and authenticated maintainer actions.

**Outputs:**

- Advise-mode feedback through one maintained report, clear status, and
  policy-directed review handoff for passed PRs.
- Stable correction requests, response tracking, bounded follow-up, and
  rescreening when relevant answers, submission content, or code change.
- Authorized reruns, overrides, waivers, guidance, proposal/PR intent acceptance,
  resolutions, appeals, audit responses, and maintainer-time recording.
- Action history and lifecycle records for triage, author waits, appeals,
  abandonment, and proposal decisions.
- Passive automated-activity annotations that cannot affect screening outcomes.

**Completion criteria:** A contributor can correct a rejected submission or appeal;
a maintainer can resolve the case with a recorded reason and scope. Acceptance
does not waive technical checks and expires when its scope changes. Labels and
unauthorized commands grant no authority. Editing or deleting a relied-on response
invalidates the affected result. Bounded follow-up and echo suppression prevent
repetitive bot replies.

## M09 — Repository admission and merge-queue verification

**Goal:** Make screening capable of enforcing admission to human review for
selected categories while preserving maintainer merge authority.

**Inputs:** M08 feedback and controls; repository branch-protection configuration;
mixed-category policies; merge-queue test cases; current admission records.

**Outputs:**

- Verified repository checks for observe, advise, and enforce, including mixed
  modes, category ambiguity, waiting states, and scoped maintainer overrides.
- Publication and reruns that cannot let stale or superseded work
  certify newer inputs or overwrite the current report.
- Explicit blocking behavior for shared PR head commits and unavailable required
  verification, plus reconciliation of abandoned checks.
- Merge-group verification against current group membership and required
  coverage, preserving member PR outcomes and the strictest applicable mode.
- Demonstrated transitions into and out of enforcement, with documented
  repository prerequisites and platform limitations.

**Completion criteria:** Integration exercises cover same-commit reruns, concurrent
updates, changed dependencies, shared heads, lost publication, and rebuilt merge
groups. Overrides cannot bypass authorization, freshness, ownership, durable
evidence, or shared-head restrictions. Unenforced categories remain nonblocking
except for the specified safety and waiting exceptions. Live enforcement remains
subject to M12's measured rollout decision.

## M10 — Submission assistant and maintainer dashboard

**Goal:** Expose requirements and screening state without requiring contributors
or maintainers to reconstruct them from raw evidence.

**Inputs:** M08 policies, reports, histories, and metrics; visibility-authorized
publication data; repository mode and submission requirements.

**Outputs:**

- A static contributor assistant that explains category requirements, checks
  draft completeness, and hands prepared issue or PR content to GitHub.
- Maintainer views for triage, awaiting-author, awaiting-approval, queued work,
  appeals, audits, and proposal backlog, with ages and changed-input indicators.
- Evidence, action history, usage, cost, and calibration views with unavailable
  information clearly identified.
- Authorized publication with GitHub action handoffs; private repositories retain
  usable evidence and Actions summaries when public export is disabled.

**Completion criteria:** Users complete submission preparation and triage tasks
against representative data. The browser holds no credentials, performs no
inference, and makes no authenticated writes. Draft guidance matches the mode.
Public exports contain only authorized material; dashboard unavailability does
not prevent evidence inspection or GitHub-based maintainer actions.

## M11 — Installable and operable release candidate

**Goal:** Let an administrator adopt, verify, maintain, and recover Patch Steward
without relying on its developers.

**Inputs:** M05 local tools; M06 replay baseline; M09 hosted admission; M10 browser
application; authorized fresh public and private test repositories.

**Outputs:**

- Versioned CLI, action/workflow, template, and browser distributions, with
  repository initialization and reproducible installation instructions.
- Installation that preserves existing repository content and exposes proposed
  changes and required administrator actions before applying them.
- End-to-end self-tests for providers, permissions, evidence access, current-check
  behavior, mixed modes, and merge queues.
- Operational guidance for resource limits, health failures, queued work, stale
  results, retention, upgrades, recovery, and disabling screening.
- A release-candidate verification record covering the supported topologies,
  providers, evidence-store options, and repository visibility combinations.

**Completion criteria:** An administrator installs from published candidate
artifacts into fresh test repositories, reaches a first observed run, and follows
the documented recovery paths. Installation starts in observe mode. Missing
provider access, unwritable evidence, and unavailable Pages have distinct visible
effects. Replay comparison and adversarial integration checks identify no
unresolved violation of the release's required behavior or trust boundaries.

## M12 — Measured rollout and version 1 acceptance

**Goal:** Establish whether the delivered system reduces net maintainer work and
which categories, if any, justify enforcement.

**Inputs:** M11 release candidate; participating repositories and maintainers;
M06 evaluation baseline; an agreed evaluation protocol and acceptance thresholds.

**Outputs:**

- A protocol fixed before outcome analysis, defining the evaluation period,
  comparison cohort, category coverage, labeling coverage, and acceptable error
  and workload levels.
- Observation and bounded feedback-pilot results, including invalid submissions
  admitted, valid contributions blocked, retries, abandonment, approval delays,
  appeals, overrides, failure rates, cost, and latency.
- Net maintainer-time comparisons that include triage, audits, appeals, policy
  upkeep, operations, and amortized setup, with missing data and uncertainty shown.
- Recorded per-category decisions to remain in observe, use advise, or enable
  enforcement, with reversal criteria and reasons for any withheld rollout.
- Final release verification, updated replay comparisons, documentation, and a
  version 1 acceptance record separating delivered capabilities from measured
  effectiveness.

**Completion criteria:** All earlier milestones satisfy their criteria. Pilot
results use exact screened revisions and an appropriate contemporaneous control
or clearly state the limits of the comparison. Enforcement is enabled only for
categories meeting the previously recorded thresholds. If evidence is insufficient
or screening adds workload, the report says so and leaves enforcement withheld
or reversed; implementation completion alone cannot establish product success.
